source_components.vertical_processing: building local Y = source orthometric height minus common 32.0 m datum; zero-height source road vertices draped to the cropped source TIN with +0.02 m display offset; cameras interpolate the TIN
source_components.road_elevation_limitations: All selected source LOD1 road heights are 0.0 and are treated as missing elevations. Only road vertices are draped to the DEM; triangulated polygon interiors are an approximation, not a terrain-clipped road surface.
source_components.scope: Modern source buildings, roads and terrain; not a single-date view of the current city or evidence of 1976 conditions.

source_components.what_supports: Publisher caption attributes the matching wide gate photograph to 1978; inspected pixels show the curved upturned silhouette, bulb arrays, a light central name panel and Suzuya on the left. It does not prove 1976 presence or paint colour.

source_components.provider: 歌舞伎町商店街振興組合事務局
source_components.what_supports: The association retrospectively associates the distinctive red arch with 1969 and says the 2013 work retained the old design, raised the structure by 0.5 m and introduced LED/solar equipment. Dimensions refer to 2013; they are a scale prior only.
source_components.rights_status: Cited research evidence only. No source photograph, aerial raster or page image is embedded; this citation grants no redistribution right in the source material.

source_components.what_supports: Museum catalogue records a photograph named Kabukicho Ichibangai on 1972-12-23. A locally inspected exhibition-panel rephotograph labelled 1972 shows a rectangular arch, but original museum-image pixel matching remains unperformed. This is a retained counterexample, not discarded evidence.
source_components.rights_status: Cited research evidence only. No source photograph, aerial raster or page image is embedded; this citation grants no redistribution right in the source material.

source_components.what_supports: The retrospective article repeats the 1969 origin of the present-style arch while also displaying a 1972-labelled rectangular predecessor. It supports street/entrance context and makes the chronological conflict explicit; it is not independent proof of the target-year form.
source_components.rights_status: Cited research evidence only. No source photograph, aerial raster or page image is embedded; this citation grants no redistribution right in the source material.

source_components.what_supports: Owner chronology records Shinjuku Toho Kaikan completion in October 1969; separates it chronologically and physically from the older Koma complex.

source_components.what_supports: Official redevelopment announcement names both Koma Theatre and Shinjuku Toho Kaikan sites; supports treating them as separate buildings.
source_components.rights_status: Cited research evidence only. No source photograph, aerial raster or page image is embedded; this citation grants no redistribution right in the source material.

source_components.what_supports: Inspected photograph shows a pale panelled long facade, rows of small windows, a deep canopy, repeated entrances and freestanding box lettering on the canopy that reads コマ東宝 and, on a second ledge, コマシネマ (corrected on r05 re-inspection; earlier records read the second string as コマ劇場). Which face of the theatre it shows is not established. Carrying these motifs into 1976 is an explicit assumption.
source_components.rights_status: Cited research evidence only. No source photograph, aerial raster or page image is embedded; this citation grants no redistribution right in the source material.

source_components.what_supports: Inspected photograph distinguishes the low Plaza Theatre front, stairs, Club Heights sign and setback tower. Right of the stairs, a windowless white wall carries a ring emblem with the latin letters KOMA, poster cases and a cinema banner ending 上映中 コマ東宝, followed by a large freestanding latin K (corrected on r05 re-inspection: the ring belongs to the Koma side, not the Toho Kaikan). Adopted as a nearby-year shape reference; programmes are not carried back.

source_years_scope: Associated source and represented-event years. Consult each component's year_role, represented_event_year, publication_year and year_range before treating a year as a photograph capture date.
processing: scripts/render_period_scene.py renders the adopted walk at recorded time 36.8762492 s using the shared model and current walk pose; scripts/assemble_completion_previews.py copies the PNG byte-for-byte. No archival photograph is copied as a billboard or texture; preserve the labelled inferred status.
inferred_elements: The user authorized a complete, coherent reconstruction hypothesis. Adoption settles production choices, not historical uncertainty. Exact gate chronology, unseen facades, dimensions, paint colours, context-building survival, plaza objects and historic surface levels remain inferred as recorded in the linked decisions.
redistribution_review: Only authored/derived geometry, configuration or rendered output is published. Cited archival photographs and source rasters are evidence only and are not republished; no photo-license grant is asserted.
appearance_reference_role: Visual colour/material target only; never counted as independent historical evidence.
